BDK p. 11

One Mind and its two gateways

BDK translationYoshito S. Hakeda

p. 11 The revelation of the true meaning [of the principle of the Mahayana can be achieved] by [unfolding the doctrine] that the principle of One Mind has two aspects.⁕ One is the aspect of Mind in terms of the absolute (tathatā; suchness), and the other is the aspect of Mind in terms of phenomena (samsara; birth and death). Each of these two aspects embraces all states of existence. Why? Because these two aspects are mutually inclusive.

Wŏnhyo · CommentaryT1844 ↗

Interpretation

2. The interpretation proper

2.3. The three divisions explained
1. Revealing the correct meaning
1.1. Explanation of what was established
1.1.1. The Dharma under discussion

Interpretation › 2. The interpretation proper › 3. The three divisions explained › 1. Revealing the correct meaning › 1. Explanation of what was established › 1. The Dharma under discussion

1.1.1.1. The general statement
One Mind and its two gateways
BDK 11 ↗One Mind has two aspects

In the general explanation, the words “the one dharma of mind has two gateways” accord with the sūtra.ᵀ “Quiescence is called One Mind. One Mind is called tathāgatagarbha.”

one dharma of mind · 一心法 yī xīn fǎ · BDK p. 11 principle of One Mind
two gateways · 二種門 èr zhǒng mén · BDK p. 11 two aspects
BDK 11 ↗Mind in terms of the absolute; Mind in terms of phenomena

The gateway of mind as suchness explains the sūtra’s “quiescence is called One Mind.”ᵀ The gateway of mind as arising and ceasing explains its “One Mind is called tathāgatagarbha.”ᵀ Why? All dharmas are without cessation. Quiescent from the beginning,ᵀ they are simply One Mind. This is called the gateway of mind as suchness. Hence “quiescence is called One Mind.”

gateway of mind as suchness · 心真如門 xīn zhēn rú mén · BDK p. 11 aspect of Mind in terms of the absolute
gateway of mind as arising and ceasing · 心生滅門 xīn shēng miè mén · BDK p. 11 aspect of Mind in terms of phenomena
All dharmas · 一切法 yī qiè fǎ · BDK p. 11 all states of existence

↥ This One Mind also has original awakening as intrinsic to its very being.ᵀ Moved by ignorance, it arises and ceases.ᵀ In this gateway, the nature of the Tathāgata lies hidden. Hence the name tathāgatagarbha. As the sūtra says, “The tathāgatagarbha is the cause of what is wholesome and unwholesome. It brings forth every kind of birth in every destiny, like an actor appearing by turns in the guise of beings in the various destinies.” Such meanings belong to the gateway of arising and ceasing. Thus “One Mind is called tathāgatagarbha” discloses this gateway of the One Mind.ᵀ

original awakening · 本覺 běn jué · BDK p. 17 original enlightenment
arises and ceases · 生滅 shēng miè · BDK p. 16 birth and death (samsara) Hakeda adds “(samsara)” when translating this passage.
gateway of arising and ceasing · 生滅門 shēng miè mén · BDK p. 11 aspect of Mind in terms of phenomena

↥ The treatise says below, “As for mind’s arising and ceasing, it is on the basis of the tathāgatagarbha that there is a mind that arises and ceases,”ᵀ and so on, down to “this consciousness has two meanings, awakening and nonawakening.”ᵀ What the gateway encompasses extends beyond the arising-and-ceasing mind alone. It takes in both the very reality of that which arises and ceases and its characteristics of arising and ceasing.ᵀ

mind’s arising and ceasing · 心生滅 xīn shēng miè · BDK p. 16 The Mind as phenomena (samsara)
two meanings · 二種義 èr zhǒng yì · BDK p. 16 two aspects
awakening · 覺義 jué yì · BDK p. 16 enlightenment
nonawakening · 不覺 bù jué · BDK p. 16 nonenlightenment
arising and ceasing · 生滅 shēng miè · BDK p. 16 birth and death (samsara) Hakeda adds “(samsara)” when translating this passage.
Why it is called One Mind
BDK 11 ↗The principle of One Mind

Such are the two gateways. What, then, is meant by “One Mind”? Defiled and pure dharmas are nondual in nature. No difference can ultimately be found between the two gateways of the true and the delusive. Hence “one.” This nonduality is what is real in all dharmas. Unlike empty space, its very nature is wondrously aware. Hence “mind.” But if there are no two, how could there be a one? If no one can be found, to what could the word “mind” refer? This truth lies beyond language and conceptual thought. We have no name for it and call it “One Mind” for want of a better term.

How each gateway encompasses all dharmas
BDK 11 ↗Each of these two aspects embraces all states of existence

“Each of these two gateways comprehends all dharmas” explains the earlier statement that this mind encompasses all mundane and supramundane dharmas. Previously the treatise simply said that mind encompasses all dharmas. Here it shows that each gateway encompasses them all.

Why the two gateways are inseparable
BDK 11 ↗Because these two aspects are mutually inclusive

“Because these two gateways are inseparable” explains how each encompasses everything.ᵀ The gateway of suchness expresses the common characteristic of the defiled and the pure. There are no separate defiled or pure dharmas apart from this common characteristic.ᵀ It can therefore encompass all defiled and pure dharmas. The gateway of arising and ceasing displays the defiled and the pure in their particularity. Nothing falls outside the scope of defiled and pure dharmas. This gateway therefore also encompasses all dharmas.ᵀ The common and the particular differ, yet each gateway excludes nothing. Hence the two are called inseparable. This completes the general explanation.

inseparable · 不相離 bù xiāng lí · BDK p. 11 mutually inclusive
gateway of suchness · 真如門 zhēn rú mén · BDK p. 11 aspect of Mind in terms of the absolute
all dharmas · 一切諸法 yī qiè zhū fǎ · BDK p. 12 all things
Wŏnhyo · Separate NotesT1845 ↗

1. The two gateways together

One Mind and the two gateways

BDK 11 ↗One Mind has two aspects

“On the basis of the dharma of One Mind there are two gateways.”ᵀ As the sūtra underlying this passage says, “Quiescence is called One Mind. One Mind is called the tathāgatagarbha.”

dharma of One Mind · 一心法 yī xīn fǎ · BDK p. 11 principle of One Mind
two gateways · 二種門 èr zhǒng mén · BDK p. 11 two aspects

  1. The expression “the gateway of mind as suchness” explains the sūtra’s “quiescence is called One Mind.”ᵀ

    gateway of mind as suchness · 心真如門 xīn zhēn rú mén · BDK p. 11 aspect of Mind in terms of the absolute

  2. “The gateway of mind as arising and ceasing” explains its “One Mind is called the tathāgatagarbha.”ᵀ

    gateway of mind as arising and ceasing · 心生滅門 xīn shēng miè mén · BDK p. 11 aspect of Mind in terms of phenomena
1. Quiescence and the gateway of suchness

↥ What does this mean? All dharmas are unborn and unceasing, originally quiescent, solely One Mind.ᵀ One Mind understood in this way is called the gateway of mind as suchness. Hence the words “quiescence is called One Mind.”

All dharmas · 一切諸法 yī qiè zhū fǎ · BDK p. 12 all things
2. Tathāgatagarbha and the gateway of arising and ceasing

↥ The essence of this One Mind is original awakening.ᵀ Yet in dependence on ignorance it moves, taking the form of arising and ceasing.ᵀ Accordingly, in this gateway the nature of a tathāgata lies concealed and does not manifest. Hence the name tathāgatagarbha. As the sūtra says, “The tathāgatagarbha is the cause of the wholesome and the unwholesome. It can bring forth all destinies of rebirth, like an actor who in turn portrays beings of every destiny.” Such meanings belong to the gateway of arising and ceasing. Thus “One Mind is called the tathāgatagarbha” brings out the gateway of the arising and ceasing of One Mind.ᵀ

original awakening · 本覺 běn jué · BDK p. 17 original enlightenment
arising and ceasing · 生滅 shēng miè · BDK p. 16 birth and death (samsara) Hakeda adds “(samsara)” when translating this passage.
gateway of the arising and ceasing of One Mind · 生滅門 shēng miè mén · BDK p. 11 aspect of Mind in terms of phenomena

↥ As the text says below, “As for mind as arising and ceasing, it is on the basis of the tathāgatagarbha that there is a mind that arises and ceases,”ᵀ and so on down to “This consciousness has two meanings, original awakening and nonawakening.”ᵀ We can see, then, that the mind that arises and ceases is only part of what this gateway comprises. It takes in both the very substance of arising and ceasing and its characteristics. All count as characteristics of arising and ceasing, all as meanings included within this gateway. The cause, the conditions, and the characteristics of arising and ceasing constitute this gateway. Such, then, is the meaning of the two gateways.

mind as arising and ceasing · 心生滅 xīn shēng miè · BDK p. 16 The Mind as phenomena (samsara)
arises and ceases · 生滅 shēng miè · BDK p. 16 birth and death (samsara) Hakeda adds “(samsara)” when translating this passage.
two meanings · 二種義 èr zhǒng yì · BDK p. 16 two aspects
nonawakening · 不覺 bù jué · BDK p. 16 nonenlightenment

Why the name “One Mind”?

↥ Why “One Mind”? The natures of defiled and pure dharmas are nondual. The gateways of the true and the delusive cannot be different. Hence “one.” This nonduality is what is real in dharmas. Its substance differs from empty space. It is by nature wondrously aware. Hence “mind.” Yet when there is no two, how could there be a one? When no one can be found, what could one call “mind”? This reality is beyond speech and conceptual thought. At a loss how to designate it, one provisionally calls it “One Mind.”

How each gateway encompasses all dharmas

BDK 11 ↗Each of the two aspects embraces all states of existence

“These two gateways each encompass all dharmas” explains the earlier proposition that this mind encompasses mundane and supramundane dharmas.ᵀ “Because the two gateways are inseparable” explains how each can encompass them all.ᵀ How so?

all dharmas · 一切法 yī qiè fǎ · BDK p. 11 all states of existence
inseparable · 不相離 bù xiāng lí · BDK p. 11 mutually inclusive
1. Suchness as the common characteristic

1. Suchness as the common characteristic

The particles and the earthenware

↥ The gateway of suchness is the common characteristic of dharmas.ᵀ No dharmas exist separately outside this common characteristic, and all are encompassed by it. For example, fine particles are the common characteristic of earthenware. There are no pots apart from this common characteristic. All the pots are encompassed by the particles. So too with the gateway of suchness.⁕

gateway of suchness · 真如門 zhēn rú mén · BDK p. 11 aspect of Mind in terms of the absolute
2. The particulars that arise and cease

2. The particulars that arise and cease

The earthenware and its particles

↥ What about the gateway of arising and ceasing? This very suchness is the cause of the wholesome and unwholesome. In conjunction with conditions it in turn becomes the various dharmas. Even as it actually takes these forms, its true nature is never impaired. This gateway therefore encompasses suchness too. Fine particles come together to form earthenware, continually retaining their nature and characteristics as particles. Thus the gateway of earthenware itself encompasses the particles. So too with arising and ceasing.

Why the two gateways are inseparable

↥ Suppose that, though the gateways had no separate substance, their characteristics conflicted and they could not interpenetrate. Then the gateway of suchness would encompass reality in principle without encompassing particular phenomena, and the gateway of arising and ceasing would encompass particular phenomena without encompassing their principle.⁕ In fact the gateways interpenetrate, with no boundary dividing them. Hence each encompasses all dharmas, principle and particulars alike. This is why the treatise says the two gateways are inseparable.

What each gateway discloses

↥ Question. If each gateway encompasses both principle and phenomena, why does the gateway of suchness disclose only the essence of the Mahāyāna, whereas the gateway of arising and ceasing discloses essence, attributes, and activity alike?

↥ Answer. To encompass differs from to disclose. How so?

The gateway of suchness

↥ The gateway of suchness effaces the characteristics to disclose reality as such. To efface the characteristics leaves them uneliminated, so the gateway encompasses them. To efface them leaves none standing as characteristics, so the gateway does not disclose them.

The gateway of arising and ceasing

↥ The gateway of arising and ceasing takes up reality as such to constitute particular phenomena. Taking it up leaves it intact, so the gateway encompasses it. Taking it up leaves it uneffaced, so this gateway also discloses the essence.

What each gateway discloses

↥ It is on these grounds that we provisionally distinguish the two. Speaking comprehensively, their two capacities are alike. Thus the gateway of suchness, too, must disclose the characteristics of particular phenomena. The treatise passes this over for brevity.

Principle and particular dharmas in the two gateways
BDK 11 ↗The two aspects are mutually inclusive

Question. We have seen how the two gateways differ. Do the principle and the particulars they encompass also differ according to the gateway?

↥ Answer. When distinguished according to gateway, they too differ. How so?

Particular dharmas
The imagined nature

↥ The particular dharmas encompassed by the gateway of suchness belong to the imagined nature. For dharmas are said to be unborn, unceasing, and originally quiescent.ᵀ Their distinctions depend solely on delusive thought.ᵀ

unborn, unceasing · 不生不滅 bù shēng bù miè · BDK p. 12 unborn and is imperishable
delusive thought · 妄念 wàng niàn · BDK p. 12 illusions
The dependent nature

↥ The particular dharmas discussed in the gateway of the arising and ceasing of mind belong to the dependent nature. For dharmas are said to arise and cease through the conjunction of causes and conditions.

How the two natures are undivided

↥ Although these two natures are not identical, neither are they different. Why? The distinctions among the arising and ceasing dharmas born of causes and conditions cannot be separated from delusive thought. Thus the imagined nature is undivided from the dependent nature and is also present in the gateway of arising and ceasing. Conversely, in conditioned arising, arising from self, from another, or from both is in every case unfindable. Thus the dependent nature is undivided from the imagined and is also present in the gateway of suchness.

How the two natures remain distinct

↥ Although these two natures are undivided, neither are they identical. Why? Dharmas of the imagined nature have never existed, nor can their absence be denied. Dharmas of the dependent nature, though lacking existence of their own, cannot be said to be absent either. The two natures therefore remain distinct.⁕ As the Compendium of the Mahāyāna says, “In their relation to one another, the three natures are undivided and yet not undivided. This is how to speak of them. If one grasps how the three natures are neither identical nor different, there is no dispute among the hundred schools one cannot reconcile.”

Principle

↥ How does the principle encompassed by the two gateways differ?

Suchness and the limit of reality

↥ In the gateway of suchness one calls it “suchness,” although it cannot be apprehended and is not nonexistent either. Whether buddhas appear or do not appear, its nature and characteristic abide, unaltered and indestructible. Within this gateway one provisionally establishes such designations as “suchness” and “the limit of reality,” as in the Larger Sūtra and other Perfection of Wisdom sūtras.

Buddha-nature and original awakening

↥ As for the principle encompassed by the gateway of arising and ceasing, although in its essence it is free of the characteristics of arising and ceasing, it does not hold fast to a nature of permanence. Conditioned by ignorance, it circulates in saṃsāra. Though it actually undergoes defilement, it is intrinsically pure.ᵀ Within this gateway one provisionally establishes such designations as “buddha-nature” and “original awakening,” as in the Nirvāṇa and Flower Garland sūtras.

intrinsically pure · 自性清淨 zì xìng qīng jìng · BDK p. 29 pure in its self-nature
Why the principle is undivided

↥ The Laṅkāvatāra and other sūtras expounded in the present treatise take both gateways together as their central purport.ᵀ These two meanings too are undivided. Although reality is free of arising and ceasing and abides permanently, even that nature cannot be grasped. Though it follows conditions, it is always unmoving, being free of a nature of arising and ceasing. For this reason, within the gateway of suchness one says simply that the true characteristic is taught without destroying provisional names,ᵀ and that the various dharmas are established without disturbing the limit of reality. In the gateway of arising and ceasing, one goes on to say that mind, intrinsically pure,ᵀ is stirred by the wind of ignorance. Undefiled, it undergoes defilement. Defiled, it remains undefiled.

both gateways · 二門 èr mén · BDK p. 11 two aspects
provisional names · 假名 jiǎ míng · Skt. prajñapti · BDK p. 13 provisional
mind, intrinsically pure · 自性清淨心 zì xìng qīng jìng xīn · BDK p. 21 Mind, pure in its own nature
Emptiness and nonemptiness
Can the two be assigned to different gateways?
BDK 11 ↗The two aspects and their respective meanings

Question. In the gateway of suchness, is emptiness alone taught,ᵀ and in the gateway of arising and ceasing, nonemptiness? Is that not how it is?ᵀ

emptiness · 空 kōng · Skt. śūnya (empty), śūnyatā (emptiness) · BDK p. 15 empty Here Wŏnhyo uses the noun “emptiness” for the aspect of suchness that Hakeda calls “empty.”
nonemptiness · 不空 bù kōng · Skt. aśūnya (nonempty) · BDK p. 15 nonempty

↥ Answer. As a first approximation, there is some truth to this pairing. That is why the preceding Outline says solely that suchness can disclose the essence of the Mahāyāna, while the gateway of arising and ceasing also discloses its attributes and activity. Strictly speaking, however, this division does not hold. In the text below nonemptiness is taught in both gateways.⁕

How can emptiness take the form of what exists?
BDK 11 ↗How each gateway encompasses all dharmas

Question. If the gateway of arising and ceasing includes both meanings, I can see how mind, insofar as it is nonempty, can arise and cease in response to conditions. But emptiness means that nothing is there. How, then, can it respond to conditions and take the form of what exists?

↥ Answer. The two meanings are one. We cannot speak of them as different. Even considered in its emptiness, mind can take the form of what exists. Why? If emptiness were fixed as emptiness, it could not take such a form. But this emptiness is itself empty, so it can.⁕

Two meanings of emptiness of emptiness

↥ This “emptiness of emptiness” in turn has two meanings.

1. In the gateway of suchness

↥ Existing things are empty by nature, and this emptiness too is empty. Neither what exists nor its emptiness can be grasped. This is the emptiness of emptiness in the gateway of suchness. As the Larger Perfection of Wisdom Sūtra says, “All dharmas are empty. This emptiness too is empty. This is called the emptiness of emptiness.”

2. In the gateway of arising and ceasing

↥ What exists has no fixed nature that makes it existent, so it can be empty. This is called “emptiness.” In the same way, this emptiness has no fixed nature that makes it empty, so it can take the form of what exists. This is called the “emptiness of emptiness.” This is the emptiness of emptiness in the gateway of arising and ceasing. As the Nirvāṇa Sūtra says, “It exists and it does not exist. This is called the emptiness of emptiness. It is so and it is not so. This is called the emptiness of emptiness. Even bodhisattvas at the tenth ground grasp only a hair’s breadth of this emptiness of emptiness. How much less could anyone else grasp?”⁕

1. The two gateways together

↥ This is how to understand the difference between the two gateways. This completes the explanation of the earlier general statement of the dharma.
